messages:
Anya - Finance: FYI — found a negative payout line in the AWS Marketplace statement for account redwood-reseller-us: -$12,340. Appears as 'chargeback/reseller_adjustment' on 2026-03-31. Export uploaded to s3://redwood-finance/marketplace/mar-2026.csv :eyes:

billing-bot: Automated: file uploaded to S3. Link: s3://redwood-finance/marketplace/mar-2026.csv (checksum available).

Mike - Infra: Can you paste the statement id and the MP transaction id? Which region did this hit?

Anya - Finance: stmt_id: AWS-2026-03-4221, txn: mp-0a1b2c3d, region: us-west-2. Quick CSV snippet below:

```
account_id,txn_id,type,amount,currency,date
redwood-reseller-us,mp-0a1b2c3d,chargeback,-12340,USD,2026-03-31
```

Sasha - EngOps: Is this tied to reserved capacity commitments? We started a reseller->direct migration for some Dedicated pools in late March.

Raj - CloudFin: Marketplace has two common flows that cause negative lines: refunds/chargebacks or commitment offset reversals when reseller contracts change. If a reseller cancels/adjusts reservations, MP can reverse earlier credits. Need to map the txn to our contract change logs and the reseller termination notice.

Anya - Finance: I pulled the reseller's notice — they reported termination for sku nvidia-a100-40g-commit on 2026-03-28. Our Dedicated telemetry still shows active capacity for that SKU until 2026-04-10. Looks like an overlap.

Mike - Infra: If we kept serving on those GPUs while the reseller was terminated in MP, the marketplace might have reclaimed credits and issued a negative payout. I'll pull provisioning logs and node lifecycle for the affected pool.

Sasha - EngOps: Found a provisioning decommission attempt on 2026-03-28 that partially failed due to a security group rule. Snippet from /var/log/prov/2026-03-28-provision.log:

```
2026-03-28T03:17:02Z INFO decommission job started pool=reseller-us-west-2 sku=nvidia-a100-40g
2026-03-28T03:17:12Z ERROR terminate-instance i-0f12ab failed: "security group sg-0abc denies outbound to marketplace callback"
2026-03-28T03:17:13Z WARN partial decommission: 3/12 nodes remained active
2026-03-28T03:17:15Z INFO reschedule decommission for remaining nodes
```

Sasha - EngOps: That partial decommission would leave some capacity still serving while MP considered the reseller terminated -> plausible root cause for chargeback.

Raj - CloudFin: I'll open a support case with AWS Marketplace (include txn mp-0a1b2c3d) and ask for a detailed ledger and reversal rationale. Also looping in legal for contract interpretation. @Anya - please attach reseller termination notice and any email threads.

Anya - Finance: Attached termination PDF and reseller invoice mapping spreadsheet to the S3 folder. Also pinged reseller-ops via email (cc: reseller-ops@partner.com).

billing-bot: Ticket created: AWS-MP-123456. Estimated response SLA 3-5 business days. Reference: mp-0a1b2c3d.

Sasha - EngOps: Short-term mitigation idea: if AWS confirms double-counting due to failed decommission, finance can post a provisional GL hold/contra entry for $12,340 pending resolution. Also we'll patch the SG rule to avoid future partial decommissions.

Mike - Infra: I'll create a follow-up infra action: run a one-off audit to reconcile node lifecycle events with MP meter events for March. Putting a task in eng-infra backlog: INFRA-3789.

Anya - Finance: :thumbsup: Starting a GL hold for $12,340. Will wait on AWS support before booking final adjustment.

Raj - CloudFin: Once AWS responds, we'll reconcile against reseller credits and decide whether to invoice reseller or absorb. Will update thread.

Sasha - EngOps: Adding a quick note — if we need to bill the reseller, we should capture per-node usage (vCPU/GPU hours) and map to the MP meter id. That mapping is in /data/usage/march-2026/marketplace_mappers.csv.

Anya - Finance: Thanks all. Leaving this on watch. I'll update after AWS reply or if reseller responds earlier.
